Despite the folder name, this dataset is NOT exports. The published measure is 'Total Waste Accepted or Exported' — UK reprocessing and export combined. The 2025 final figure of 7,794,043 tonnes matches the quarterly dataset's combined total of 7,795,720 to within 1,677 tonnes, 0.02 per cent, and that gap is explained by extraction date: this file was taken on 10 February 2026 and the quarterly Q4 file on 30 March 2026. To split UK reprocessing from export, use the quarterly dataset, which reports the two separately. Treating this file as export tonnage would overstate exports by roughly a factor of two.

The thirteen sheets per file are CUMULATIVE totals from 1 January to each cut-off date, not monthly increments. Summing the sheets would multiply the year's tonnage roughly sevenfold. The monthly flow is the difference between consecutive snapshots, which is what clean/export_flows_increments_clean.csv provides.

Between 9.9 and 11.6 per cent of each year's final tonnage was not on the database when the compliance year closed: 812,240 tonnes for 2023, 942,811 for 2024 and 882,032 for 2025. By material in 2025 the lag runs from 8.6 per cent for aluminium to 14.3 per cent for wood. This corroborates the January-window finding in the quarterly dataset from a different measure — tonnage entered rather than evidence issued — and means any figure quoted before roughly February of the following year is provisional by about a tenth.

The 2024 filename carries a '_(6)' suffix added by the browser on download, not by the regulator. Left as downloaded so the file on disk matches the manifest hash; it has no effect on parsing, which reads the compliance year from the 'Recycling_2024_Monthly_Report' portion.
